paragraphs.text: As being too light of belief: the lies of the spies they took for oracles.
paragraphs.anchor: And the people wept that night.

paragraphs.text: Words of deep discontent, despair, and unthanklulness.
paragraphs.anchor: Would God that we had died.

paragraphs.text: How could that be better? It is our wisest way, to crush the very first insurrections of unruly passions (do not great storms rise out of little gusts?); to smother the smoke thereof, which else will fume up into the head, and gather into so thick a cloud, as we shall soon lose the sight of ourselves, and what is best to be done.
paragraphs.anchor: Were it not better for us to return into Egypt.

paragraphs.text: Thus they proceeded from bad to worse. Passions, like heavy bodies down steep hills, once in motion move themselves, and know no ground but the bottom. Whether this people did make them such a captain, for such a purpose, is uncertain; but howsoever their very intention of doing it, is charged upon them, as if they had done it. {Neh 9:16-17}
What they said unto them see Deu 1:29-30. See also on Num 16:15.
And wept, saith Sulpitius.

q.d., We shall make but a breakfast of them. So that valiant Prince of Orange told his soldiers at the battle of Newport, when they had the sea on the one side, and the Spaniards on the other, that they must either eat up those Spaniards, or drink up that sea.
This is merces mundi, this is the fruit of ochlocratie, that rule of rascality, as one calls it.
paragraphs.anchor: But all the congregation bade stone them.

paragraphs.text: Unbelief is the root of rebellion and apostasy. {Heb 3:12}

Here God offered Moses a private fortune, which he prudently refuseth, because God should be a loser by it. And surely, saith a divine, as God was displeased with Balsam for going, though he bade him go: so the Lord would not have taken it so kindly of Moses if he had taken him upon the offer he made in a time of his heat, against his people.
paragraphs.anchor: And I will make of thee a greater nation.

paragraphs.text: And they will soon make comedies out of the Church’s tragedies.
paragraphs.anchor: Then the Egyptians shall hear it.

paragraphs.text: The proverb is, Oculus et fama non patiuntur iocos, A man’s eye and his good name can bear no jests. And he {a} was no fool that said, Negligere quid de se quisque dicat, non solum arrogantis est, sed et dissolati, He shall pass for a proud fool that makes no matter what men say of him. God is most tender of his glory; and we must take heed how we cast any slur upon it; for we quarter arms, as it were, with God.
{a} Cicero.

As he can quickly do, with a turn of his hand, with a nod of his head, {Psa 80:16} with a breath of his nostrils. {Job 4:9} He can as soon do it, as bid it be done, "whether it be done against a nation, or against a man only." {Job 34:29}
paragraphs.anchor: Kill all this people as one man.

paragraphs.text: In multiplying pardons, {Isa 55:8} in passing by the many and bony, or "mighty sins of" {a} this people, such sins as none else could or would pardon: "For who is a God like unto thee, that pardoneth such iniquity?" &c. {Mic 7:18} Hebricians have observed, that in the word jidgal here used in the original text, there is a great jod, which in numbering is ten, to show, that if the people should murmur ten times more against God than they had done, yet out of tender respect to his own great name, which would otherwise be basely blasphemed, he should pardon and spare them. {Hebrew Text Note}
paragraphs.anchor: Let the power of my Lord be great.

paragraphs.text: {a} Amo 5:12. Heb., Bony sins, fortia peccata.

This last letter in God’s dreadful name ought much to be marked. God may pardon men’s sins, and yet lay it on their skin, to humble themselves, and to warn others. "Thou forgavest them, though thou tookest vengeance of their inventions." {Psa 99:8}
paragraphs.anchor: And by no means clearing the guilty.

paragraphs.text: God’s power pleaded, {Num 14:17} and his mercy here are the Jachin and the Boaz whereon faith resteth.
paragraphs.anchor: According to the greatness of thy mercy.

paragraphs.text: viz., So as not utterly, and at once, to extirpate them. I will be "as a moth" unto them, and not as a devouring lion. {Hos 5:12; Hos 5:14}
This is an oath, as appears by comparing herewith Psa 95:11. To blame therefore are they that use it so often.
paragraphs.anchor: But as truly as I live.

paragraphs.text: I will make me a great name abroad; and even of those maidservants, the heathens, which thou hast spoken of, shall I be had in honour, as he said in another case. {2Sa 6:22}
paragraphs.anchor: All the earth shall be filled.

paragraphs.text: Let us go up and possess it, saith he. {Num 13:30} As if it were no more than to go and see and conquer. {a} A free spirit is enkindled with that which quencheth others: as when a bowl runs downhill, every bounce quickens it, whereas if uphill, it would slug it.
Heb., Hath fulfilled after me. {b} A metaphor from a ship under sail, carried strongly with the wind, as fearing neither rocks nor sands.
Personal goodness is profitable to posterity. Who would not serve such a Lord?
{a} Veni, Vidi, Vici. I came, I saw, I conquered!
{a} Implevit post me.

There was but a mountain between: so they were close by the Promised Land, and yet could not enter because of unbelief. Thou art not far from God’s kingdom? the greater is thine unhappiness, that fallest from so high hopes.
Since you have such a mind to it, you shall have enough of it. "The backslider in heart shall be filled with his own ways." {Pro 14:14}
paragraphs.anchor: By the way of the Red Sea.

paragraphs.text: God took them at their words: so he may well do our desperate swearers, since the mercy they desire God to show is to damn them. This self-cursing seldom escapeth God’s visible vengeance: witness those Jews of old, who cried, "His blood be on us," &c., besides many others of late that might be instanced. Mr Perkins tells of certain English soldiers in King Edward VI’s time, who were cast upon the French shore by a storm, in which stress they went to prayer, that they might be delivered; but one soldier among the rest, instead of praying, cried out, Gallows take thy right, or claim thy due: when he came home he was hanged indeed. So was Sir Gervaise Ellowayes, Lieutenant of the Tower in King James’ time, whose usual word at his playing at cards and dice had been, as he sorrowfully confessed at the gallows, I would I might be hanged if it be not so or so. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: So will I do to you.

paragraphs.text: {a} Looking glass for Malignants.

Cadaver a cadendo; πρωμα παρα το πιπτειν. Who knows whether God purpose not to wear out this generation, that hath been defiled with the superstitions of the land we live in, that we may not see the good that he will bring upon this Church!
i.e., Ye shall find to your cost, what it is to charge me with breach of promise, through unbelief.
God gave them somewhat to cry for.
Here was confession of sin, without confusion for sin. So was that of Saul. {1Sa 15:30}
To be out of God’s precincts, is to be out of his protection.
